scope: Proposition 11 (Power-width interchange with rows) of the manuscript “Integer multiplication below n log n” (preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 109 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 834f644c3ce67932), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the fixed circuit data satisfy (11), and let q be a prime as in Lemma 10 for its edge matrices, also avoiding the denominators of every assigned terminal and gate matrix M. Choose a rational number τ ∈ (0, 1) with s/W < mτ . For every e = mk, k ≥ 0, consider two disjoint contiguous address chunks of e radix-q digits each. Suppose a row field preceding both chunks has length divisible by Wk. There may be additional fields before and after the row field, between the chunks, and after them. The chunks can be interchanged in O(V eτ ) time, preserving every other address field, on a fixed number of finite-alphabet tapes. The constant is independent of all field lengths and of the data.
